title: Knowledge check: Streaming Responses and Server-Sent Events

questions.prompt: In Streaming Responses and Server-Sent Events, which statement best describes Stream-based response concepts?
options: Keep the interface predictable for its client: use clear resource boundaries, explicit request/response formats, correct status codes, validation and tests for failure cases.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Use asynchronous I/O for waiting work, but remember synchronous CPU-heavy functions still block the event loop. Bound concurrent work and honor cancellation, streams and backpressure.
questions.answer_key: Use asynchronous I/O for waiting work, but remember synchronous CPU-heavy functions still block the event loop. Bound concurrent work and honor cancellation, streams and backpressure.
questions.explanation: Use asynchronous I/O for waiting work, but remember synchronous CPU-heavy functions still block the event loop. Bound concurrent work and honor cancellation, streams and backpressure.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Streaming Responses and Server-Sent Events?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Node handles I/O asynchronously, but CPU-heavy work can block the event loop. Measure latency and error rates, limit work, tune data access, control cache freshness, and design backpressure and shutdown behavior.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
questions.answer_key: Node handles I/O asynchronously, but CPU-heavy work can block the event loop. Measure latency and error rates, limit work, tune data access, control cache freshness, and design backpressure and shutdown behavior.
questions.explanation: Node handles I/O asynchronously, but CPU-heavy work can block the event loop. Measure latency and error rates, limit work, tune data access, control cache freshness, and design backpressure and shutdown behavior.

questions.prompt: A change related to Streaming Responses and Server-Sent Events appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
